title: id-events: preserve empty event bodies across range sync

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

PR #7657's range-sync record frames the event as a length-prefixed header followed by raw body bytes. The decoder treats an empty remainder as `None`. The store accepts a present empty body (`Some([])`) when its signed header commits to BLAKE3(empty) and size 0, so range sync turns that valid body into a header-only event. The receiver's `event_body` then returns `MissingBody`.

The ambiguity is still present on current main in `pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/event_store/sync.rs`: `encode_record` appends no bytes for either `None` or `Some(&[])`, and `decode_record` maps every empty remainder to `None`. The later sync hardening in PR #11265 added device-operation delivery coverage with a non-empty body but did not change this framing.

## Acceptance

- The range-sync record format distinguishes an absent body from a present empty body.
- A header-only event still arrives without a body; a present empty body arrives as `Some([])` and reads back byte-identically; a non-empty body also remains byte-identical.
- The receiver continues to verify the body against the signed header's payload hash and size before storing it.
- Add tests with an explicit oracle for all three cases, including an empty payload whose header commits to BLAKE3(empty) and size 0.

## Evidence

- Merged PR #7657 introduced `encode_record` / `decode_record` and generic body range sync; the event-body issue #4837 is closed.
- Current main still decodes an empty body remainder as `None`; no later merged change to the record framing was found. PR #11265 tests a non-empty device-operation body.
- No existing issue for present-empty event bodies in range sync was found in the current issue search.

## Scope

Fix the range-sync record framing and its event-store tests. Preserve the existing batch transaction and header commitment checks. Do not change the event body format or the one-time store migration.
